doc.title: Roscoe Mitchell interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 23, 2023

title: Art Ensemble in California and Paris, and Lester Bowie
summary: He recalls Claude Delcloo's invitation to Paris, the Mill Valley house with Nick Gravenites, Lester Bowie's big ideas and selling his possessions to go to Europe, and plans for duets with Don Moye.

bands.name: Big Brother and the Holding Company

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah. When the Art Ensemble went to Paris for a couple of years, can you share what the motivation was? Was it audience? Was there any racial considerations about going abroad?

No. No. Claude Delcloo reached out to the ACM and was asking about information about going there. And I mean like we had already been to California two times in a row you know. So but that was interesting as well because the first time we went there it was with Lester Bowie and Philip Wilson and myself. And Nick Gravenitis was there doing, managing Big Brother and the Holding Company with Ron Polte. And I did a recording with Nick Gravenitis before, you know, he went out to California, “My Baby’s Got a Whole Lot of Soul” it’s called. So they had a house out there that they had got for Mike Bloomfield I believe it was and Buddy Guy — not Buddy Guy, God — Buddy Miles you know. They were going to put together a band. But they weren’t living in the house for another 30 days so they gave us the house. It was in Mill Valley. So we lived there and we had a couple of records out then and I believe “Sound” was out and also “Lester Bowie’s Numbers One and Two” were out. So we would go over to Mill Valley and practice and then we were running out of money we would go into San Francisco and sell some CDs and stuff and then go back to Mill Valley. And by the way we were out there in Lester Bowie’s — let’s see now there’s Rolls Royce — oh Bentley. There was a Bentley, a green Bentley. Lester lived large, big, always big ideas you know. Just full of them you know. I mean like when we were getting ready to go to Europe he took out an ad in the Chicago Defender and said, you know, musician sells out. And what he was doing was selling all of his furniture and everything, his possessions, to take the band to Europe you know. That’s what he did you know. Lester Bowie, wow, always full of big ideas. Big ideas. You know, encouraging and so on. So I mean like when Lester left I was faced with the question well why didn’t I ask Lester this, why didn’t I ask Lester that and so on like that you know. So yeah, it’s been a journey you know. And Malachi [Favors],

oh my God you know all of these people in the Art Ensemble. I mean Joseph. So now Don [Moye] and myself, we may start to do some duet concerts so that’s the thing that we’re thinking about right now. And then that’s — that’s the way we had talked about the Art Ensemble you know we said the Art Ensemble is the Art Ensemble until the last person standing is gone you know. So we had discussed that so it was already forecast in a way.
